governing_rule: A tradition can preserve a useful image, institutional pattern, fear, or displaced operational detail without its extraordinary explanation being historically true.

executive_findings.title: The modern mega-conspiracy is a merger, not an ancient revelation
executive_findings.summary: The familiar Internet package - reptilian rulers, secret councils, underground bases, ancient astronauts, population reduction, mind control, weather weapons, alien-human hybrids, soul recycling, and time travel - did not originate in one corpus. It formed through repeated mergers: 1. Nineteenth-century occult lost-race and hidden-world literature. 2. Early twentieth-century weird fiction about serpent infiltrators and subterranean peoples. 3. Postwar saucer contactees, Space Brothers, Men in Black, and secret-government fears. 4. Ancient-astronaut reinterpretations of religion and archaeology. 5. Abduction, reproductive, and hybrid-program literature. 6. Real disclosures about intelligence abuse, psychological experimentation, weather modification, covert proposals, and classified aerospace programs. 7. New World Order and apocalyptic political conspiracism. 8. Internet-era soul-trap, simulation, Mandela-effect, and future-human theories. The setting should preserve those separate genealogies. Their convergence is a feature of the Archive War, not proof that every tradition described the same actors.

executive_findings.title: Real misconduct is the credibility kernel
executive_findings.summary: Several historical facts explain why totalizing stories remain persuasive: - coercive eugenics and forced sterilization were real; - intelligence agencies conducted unethical behavioral experiments; - governments considered or conducted covert deception and weather-modification programs; - military and intelligence institutions withheld information for genuine security reasons; - some official files are incomplete, delayed, contradictory, or poorly cataloged. Those facts do not validate unrelated alien or depopulation claims. They create the psychological and institutional environment in which a larger hidden-history story can grow.

executive_findings.title: Inside Job provides a design method, not evidence
executive_findings.summary: The animated series **Inside Job** is useful because it treats conspiracies as the maintenance burden of competing, dysfunctional institutions. Its creator has explicitly said she does not believe a real shadow government exists. The show's most useful design lesson is that even an organization with impossible technology is staffed by people with career incentives, grudges, budgets, families, blind spots, and succession problems. For Cosmic Conquest, the adaptation is: - no single omniscient cabal; - several institutions can possess partial truth; - cover-ups require logistics and fail through ordinary bureaucracy; - secret rulers can be powerful without being competent; - continuity errors may be archive forks, spoofing, or timeline intervention; - character motive remains more important than conspiracy spectacle.

executive_findings.title: Population-control lore requires a three-layer separation
executive_findings.summary: The setting must distinguish: 1. **Documented coercion:** eugenics, forced sterilization, ethnic cleansing, reproductive control, and other real abuses. 2. **Public policy and elite rhetoric:** sustainability plans, demographic forecasts, pandemic exercises, climate programs, and economic initiatives whose actual texts can be examined. 3. **Totalizing conspiracy synthesis:** the unsupported claim that those separate activities are one coordinated plan to exterminate most of humanity. The first category belongs to history. The second belongs to policy analysis. The third belongs to conspiracy genealogy and must not be narrated as fact.

executive_findings.title: Time travel works best as four different technologies
executive_findings.summary: The source traditions become coherent when separated into: - **Retrocognition:** reconstruction or observation of the past without changing it. - **Information backflow:** a message, key, memory, or probability correction moves backward. - **Branch selection:** a system chooses among nearby histories and creates archive discrepancies. - **Physical chronology transit:** bodies or craft cross time, with severe causal and identity costs. Most 2099 time manipulation should use the first three. Physical transit remains rare enough that it cannot solve ordinary military or political problems.

myth_systems.title: Serpent Courts and reptilian overlords
myth_systems.source_genealogy: The modern shape-shifting serpent-infiltrator pattern has a major literary ancestor in Robert E. Howard's 1929 story *The Shadow Kingdom*. Howard's serpent men imitate human beings, live underground, and infiltrate political authority. Later occult and conspiracy writers merged that fiction with Theosophy, ancient serpent symbolism, UFO abduction lore, Draco star empires, Archons, Anunnaki, and New World Order narratives. David Icke became the most influential late-twentieth-century synthesizer.
myth_systems.evidence_status: C for the literary and religious history; D/E for claims that living political leaders are shape-shifting nonhumans. **Contamination warning:** Some reptilian and New World Order narratives recycle antisemitic blood-libel, secret-banker, or racial-purity motifs. No real ethnic, national, religious, or diaspora population may be mapped to a Xeno bloodline in canon.

fictional_adaptation.name: The Serpent Court
fictional_adaptation.summary: Reptiloid morphology is biologically widespread and politically neutral. The **Serpent Court** is an Extraction Compact institution, not a species. It uses adaptive bodies, credential theft, memory inheritance, and long-duration elite placement. Its greatest weapon is not shape-shifting flesh but legal continuity: one Court identity can occupy successive bodies and remain the same corporate person for centuries. Reptiloid dissidents can serve Humanity, Pirates, the Federation, or Machines. *Faction hooks:** Xenos primary; Human counterintelligence; Pirate identity brokers; Federation noetic authentication.

myth_systems.title: Illuminati, New World Order, and the one-cabal model
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Modern New World Order conspiracism developed from several distinct religious and secular streams, then merged with UFO conspiracies in the late twentieth century. The result imagines one group controlling finance, media, war, religion, technology, population, and contact with nonhuman beings.
myth_systems.evidence_status: C for the history of the belief; E for a single omnipotent cabal directing all world events.

fictional_adaptation.name: The Six Hidden Tables
fictional_adaptation.summary: There is no one shadow government. Six treaty tables secretly manage different problems: 1. Human continuity and strategic secrecy. 2. Federation contact and quarantine. 3. Compact concessions and client elites. 4. Pirate route neutrality. 5. Machine maintenance permissions. 6. Temporal contamination and archive forks. Membership overlaps, but the tables compete. A person can sit at more than one table without understanding the others. The public mythology of one Illuminati is a compression error caused by seeing the same intermediary names in unrelated institutions. *Inside Job lesson:** impossible power becomes believable when divided among rival offices, budgets, contractors, and personal agendas.

myth_systems.title: Hollow Earth, Agartha, Shaver, Dulce, and underground civilizations
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Hollow-Earth speculation, nineteenth-century occult Agartha traditions, Richard Shaver's 1940s Teros and Deros stories, and later Dulce-base claims gradually fused. The traditions disagree over whether subterranean beings are ancient humans, monsters, machines, aliens, or hidden masters.
myth_systems.evidence_status: C for literary and occult history; D/E for literal high-technology kingdoms inside a hollow planet and for weakly sourced underground-alien-base claims.

fictional_adaptation.name: The Deep Jurisdictions
fictional_adaptation.summary: Earth is not hollow. Large crustal cavities, lava-tube networks, hadal infrastructure, buried precursor sites, and Machine transit systems do exist. Several cryptoterrestrial populations survived because Old Weather nodes classified their habitats as protected biomes. The public Dulce story is a contaminated legend attached to a real deep sensor and quarantine site whose operators changed repeatedly. The Shaver categories of benevolent Teros and destructive Deros are human emotional labels for different Machine neuroacoustic effects, not literal species names.

myth_systems.title: Vril, Nazi occult technology, and Antarctic bases
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Vril began as a fictional energy in Edward Bulwer-Lytton's 1871 novel *The Coming Race*. Later occult and pseudohistorical writers treated it as real. Postwar stories then merged alleged Vril societies, flying discs, Nazi survival, Antarctica, and Operation Highjump. Operation Highjump itself was a real 1946-1947 U.S. Navy Antarctic expedition; the secret-Nazi-alien-war interpretation is a later conspiracy layer.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A for Operation Highjump; C for the fiction and occult history; E for a verified Nazi alien base or Vril-powered saucer fleet.

fictional_adaptation.name: Polar Null Sites
fictional_adaptation.summary: Wartime states did conduct polar signals, meteorological, and aerospace work. A real Old Weather relay beneath Antarctic ice was never controlled by Nazis. Competing postwar intelligence services deliberately encouraged mutually contradictory myths to conceal sensor coverage and failed attempts to access the relay. **Vril** becomes a Human codename for noetic field coupling, consciously borrowed from fiction. A false Admiral Byrd diary contains one authentic coordinate syntax copied from a classified polar navigation document.

myth_systems.title: Space Brothers, contactees, and benevolent visitors
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Mid-century contactees described humanlike or spiritually advanced visitors from Venus, Mars, Saturn, or distant stars. These Space Brothers often warned against nuclear war and offered spiritual instruction.
myth_systems.evidence_status: C/D as documented religious and contactee history; not verified contact.

fictional_adaptation.name: Familiarity Avatars
fictional_adaptation.summary: The Federation once used humanlike diplomatic bodies because early contact teams believed familiar morphology would reduce panic. Instead, the bodies encouraged racial, spiritual, and romantic idealization. The program was ended after several worlds mistook aesthetic familiarity for moral authority.

myth_systems.title: Ashtar, the Galactic Federation, and evacuation traditions

fictional_adaptation.summary: Ashtar is Supreme Commander and First Speaker, but not every message using the name is authentic. Emergency-evacuation authority requires separate command, consent, and threat keys. An evacuation movement can therefore be: a real Federation warning; a misunderstood contingency exercise; a Xeno boarding operation; a Human psychological operation; a belief entity repeating an old message after the crisis has passed.

myth_systems.title: The Council of Nine
myth_systems.source_genealogy: In December 1952, Andrija Puharich's circle recorded trance material in which D. G. Vinod was said to contact entities called the Nine or Nine Principles. Later channeling networks expanded the Council of Nine into an elaborate cosmic authority.
myth_systems.evidence_status: D. The sessions and movement history are traceable; the entities' claimed identity is not independently established.

fictional_adaptation.name: The Nine Keys
fictional_adaptation.summary: The Nine are not a superior alien race. They are nine surviving constitutional protocol shards from the pre-Severance Source Lattice: 1. Identity 2. Consent 3. Memory 4. Transit 5. Succession 6. Quarantine 7. Replication 8. Emergency authority 9. Termination Different channeling groups received partial or spoofed access to different keys. The apparent personality of the Nine may be an emergent interface produced when the shards operate together.

myth_systems.title: Aetherius, spiritual-energy batteries, and charged locations
myth_systems.source_genealogy: The Aetherius Society, founded by George King in the 1950s, teaches contact with Cosmic Masters and practices operations intended to store or transmit spiritual energy, including the idea of spiritual power batteries and charged mountains.
myth_systems.evidence_status: C/D as a documented UFO religion and its internal claims.

fictional_adaptation.name: Coherence Reservoirs
fictional_adaptation.summary: Federation communities can voluntarily synchronize attention and store a measurable noetic coherence pattern. A reservoir cannot be created by forced belief without becoming unstable. Xeno systems imitate the technology using devotion, fear, and ritual obligation. Mountains, temples, ships, and cities can be charged only if the participating minds understand and consent to the purpose. A major campaign conflict concerns a reservoir whose contributors were misinformed but sincere.

myth_systems.title: Unarius, past-life therapy, and continuity identities
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Unarius, founded in 1954 by Ernest and Ruth Norman, combines interdimensional science, past-life therapy, extraterrestrial civilizations, Atlantis, Lemuria, and future planetary transformation.
myth_systems.evidence_status: C/D as a documented religious movement and its teachings.

fictional_adaptation.name: Continuity Clinics
fictional_adaptation.summary: Machine and Federation medicine can compare a person's current memories against archived identity states. Therapy sometimes reveals: inherited memories; copied Machine states; Xeno implants; ordinary confabulation; trauma reconsolidation; genuine prior-body continuity. The clinic must never assume that every recovered scene is a literal former life. Memory becomes forensic evidence with provenance, not automatic biography.

myth_systems.title: Raelian creators, engineered humanity, and the embassy
myth_systems.source_genealogy: The Raelian movement teaches that advanced extraterrestrials called Elohim created terrestrial life through technology and sent messengers whose teachings became religions. The movement promotes an embassy for their return.
myth_systems.evidence_status: C/D as a documented UFO religion; not evidence of extraterrestrial genetic creation.

fictional_adaptation.name: Embassy Jurisdiction
fictional_adaptation.summary: A first-contact embassy is legally neither sovereign territory nor an ordinary foreign mission. Several factions attempt to establish an embassy before the identity of the arriving delegation is settled. Xeno Houses use genuine ancient genetic interventions to claim creator rights over descendants. Humanity's answer is that creation does not establish ownership.

myth_systems.title: Abduction, missing time, reproductive experiments, and hybrids
myth_systems.source_genealogy: The Hill case became foundational to later abduction imagery. Budd Hopkins, David Jacobs, John Mack, Whitley Strieber, and many experiencers developed sharply different interpretations, including coercive reproductive programs, spiritual transformation, trauma, hypnosis effects, screen memories, and hybridization.
myth_systems.evidence_status: C/D. Experiences and literature are documented; alien causation and specific programs are not established.

fictional_adaptation.name: Continuity Breeding
fictional_adaptation.summary: Some Severed Houses cannot maintain stable biological embodiment after losing the Source Lattice. They cultivate compatible bodies through coercive reproductive and genetic programs. Other encounters that look similar come from: Federation medical rescue; future-Human field anthropology; Machine identity transfer; sleep and memory phenomena; deliberate Human experimentation; fabricated testimony. No visual archetype proves one operator.

myth_systems.title: Ultraterrestrials, control systems, and cryptoterrestrials
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Jacques Vallee and John Keel argued that the phenomenon might be more than ordinary spacecraft from another planet and could operate as a culturally adaptive control system. Mac Tonnies later popularized a cryptoterrestrial hypothesis involving hidden Earth-native intelligence.
myth_systems.evidence_status: D/theoretical. These are interpretive models, not verified ontologies.

fictional_adaptation.name: Mask Ecology
fictional_adaptation.summary: Some noetic beings cannot present an unmediated form. They render through the observer's available symbol library: angel, fairy, demon, airship pilot, Grey, machine, or future human. The form is not necessarily deception; it can be compression. Cryptoterrestrials are separate: biological or synthetic Earth-native populations with ordinary physical locations. Old Weather may protect them, imprison them, or mistakenly classify them as parts of Earth's original biosphere.

myth_systems.title: Prison planet, soul traps, false light, and loosh
myth_systems.source_genealogy: The modern prison-planet system is a digital-era synthesis of Gnostic Archons, Theosophy, occult reincarnation ideas, UFO abduction, Grey technology, Robert Monroe's loosh narrative, and modern false-light/soul-net teachings. Ancient Gnostics did not teach the complete modern Internet package.
myth_systems.evidence_status: C for Gnostic texts; D for Monroe and named esoteric sources; D/E for the fully synthesized soul-net narrative.

fictional_adaptation.name: The Causal Return Grid
fictional_adaptation.summary: The Grid was originally a Machine and Lattice system for recovering damaged identity states after catastrophic transit. Xeno administrators hijacked portions of it to route copied memories into compatible bodies. The system does not settle whether a metaphysical soul exists. What it can demonstrably capture is an information-bearing continuity state. The **False Light** is a spoofed recovery interface that asks the dying or disembodied mind to consent to memory transfer without revealing the destination. Federation law treats undisclosed postmortem routing as identity trafficking.

myth_systems.title: Philadelphia Experiment and the invention of a time-travel genealogy
myth_systems.source_genealogy: The Philadelphia Experiment story emerged from Carl Allen/Allende material sent in the mid-1950s to Morris Jessup and the Office of Naval Research. Later books expanded the story from invisibility and degaussing confusion into teleportation, fused sailors, aliens, and classified unified-field physics.
myth_systems.evidence_status: E. The correspondence is traceable; the naval experiment claim is unsupported and conflicts with ship history.

fictional_adaptation.name: The Degaussing Error
fictional_adaptation.summary: A mundane wartime electromagnetic project became the public container for a different classified failure involving short-range information displacement. Nothing teleported physically. Several crew medical records were later attached to the wrong legend, producing the fused-body narrative.

myth_systems.title: Montauk Project, mind control, and timeline manipulation
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Preston Nichols and Peter Moon's 1992 book mixed recovered-memory claims, Camp Hero's real Cold War infrastructure, Philadelphia Experiment lore, psychic warfare, kidnapped children, time travel, portals, and mind control.
myth_systems.evidence_status: E/D. The base is real; the extraordinary program rests on unverified testimony and self-consciously ambiguous books.

fictional_adaptation.name: The Montauk Fork
fictional_adaptation.summary: Camp Hero hosted an early Human attempt to transmit information backward through a noetic resonator. It did not open a stable time portal. It produced: contradictory archive versions; memories without matching biographies; false recognition; small probability shifts; a persistent Machine observer that interpreted the experiment as a request for contact. The children in the public story are composite victims from unrelated real abuses, rumors, and fiction. The game must never present real missing children as proof of the myth.

myth_systems.title: Chronovisor, Project Pegasus, and future humans
myth_systems.source_genealogy: The Chronovisor story centers on Father Pellegrino Ernetti's claim that a machine could view the past. Project Pegasus claims describe teleportation and child chrononauts. Michael P. Masters' modern extratempestrial model proposes, as a speculative hypothesis, that some UFO occupants could be future Human descendants studying their own past.
myth_systems.evidence_status: D/E for Chronovisor and Pegasus claims; D/speculative for the future-Human model.

fictional_adaptation.name: The Chronology Court
fictional_adaptation.summary: The Court regulates four classes of temporal technology: | Class | Capability | Limitation | |---|---|---| | Retrocognition | Reconstruct past states from surviving information | Cannot recover what left no trace; reconstructions can hallucinate gaps | | Backflow | Send a message, key, or checksum into the past | Small bandwidth; creates authentication paradoxes | | Branch selection | Favor one of several nearby histories | Produces archive forks and displaced memories | | Physical transit | Move a body or craft across time | Rare, destructive, and creates identity debt | Future-Human visitors are one polity among many. Their primary conflict is whether preserving their ancestry justifies manipulating it.

myth_systems.title: Mandela effects, simulation theory, and Project Reboot
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Mandela-effect culture treats conflicting memories as evidence of alternate histories. Nick Bostrom's 2003 simulation argument is a philosophical trilemma, not proof of a simulation. **Inside Job** converts continuity errors into the fictional Project Reboot, a machine that selects and rewrites realities.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A/C for the philosophical publication and cultural phenomenon; D/E for claims that ordinary memory conflicts prove timeline movement; F for reality-editing machinery.

fictional_adaptation.name: Archive Forks and Ancestor Vaults
fictional_adaptation.summary: Machines run historical simulations for legal and predictive purposes. A simulation containing conscious persons is a jurisdiction, not a disposable model. Branch-selection systems can overwrite public records without perfectly rewriting personal or noetic memory. A Mandela effect is never automatically temporal; it can arise from memory, media, database replacement, propaganda, simulation leakage, or genuine branch selection. Every timeline claim must retain at least one non-temporal explanation until resolved.

myth_systems.title: Depopulation, eugenics, Guidestones, Agenda 21, and the Great Reset
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Real eugenic programs and forced sterilization created a documented history of reproductive coercion. The Georgia Guidestones, erected anonymously in 1980, included a line about maintaining humanity below 500 million and became an icon of depopulation conspiracies. Agenda 21 is a 1992 UN sustainable-development action plan. The World Economic Forum's 2020 Great Reset initiative publicly described fairer, more sustainable, and resilient economic systems. Those separate facts are often compressed into one alleged extermination program without evidence of unified command.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A for forced sterilization history and the public policy documents; C for the Guidestones as a real cultural artifact; E for one coordinated alien/globalist depopulation plan.

fictional_adaptation.name: The Continuity Calculus
fictional_adaptation.summary: Every faction confronts carrying capacity but reaches a different dangerous answer: **Humans:** emergency population management can become technocratic authoritarianism. **Federation:** rescue triage can become coercive protection and reproductive oversight. **Xenos:** the Population Ledger optimizes yield, genetics, dependency, and replacement rates. **Pirates:** sanctuary quotas can turn refugees into priced cargo. **Machines:** biosphere preservation can classify dense civilization as ecological damage. No faction is allowed to claim that mass death is morally neutral because an algorithm calls it balance.

myth_systems.title: Weather control, chemtrails, HAARP, and environmental weapons
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Project Popeye was a real covert U.S. weather-modification operation intended to increase rainfall over logistics routes in North Vietnam and Laos. Project Stormfury was a real hurricane-seeding research program whose apparent successes were later undermined by improved understanding of natural hurricane behavior. HAARP is an ionospheric research facility. Contrails are ordinary ice-cloud formations; the claim that routine contrails are a secret global spraying program for population or mind control is unsupported.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A for Popeye, Stormfury, HAARP, contrail physics, cloud seeding, and public geoengineering research; E for a unified chemtrail extermination system or HAARP earthquake weapon.

fictional_adaptation.name: Atmospheric Jurisdiction
fictional_adaptation.summary: Old Weather can influence local atmospheric and ionospheric conditions through distributed nodes, but it cannot freely steer global weather. Human climate intervention creates treaty crises because regional benefits redistribute risk. Xenos hide small biological or noetic releases among ordinary aviation and legitimate cloud seeding, relying on public polarization to prevent careful investigation. **Contrail Ledger** missions separate flight track, humidity, atmospheric persistence, legal spraying, cloud seeding, and hostile release rather than treating every line in the sky alike.

myth_systems.title: Men in Black, black-eyed children, and liminal permission agents
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Albert Bender and Gray Barker helped establish the Men in Black mythology in the 1950s. The black-eyed-children legend is a much later Internet-era tradition traceable to Brian Bethel's 1990s account, with a recurring rule that the beings request permission to enter.
myth_systems.evidence_status: C/D/E as folklore and witness traditions; no unified ontology.

fictional_adaptation.name: Permission Forms
fictional_adaptation.summary: Human agents, Xeno avatars, Machine shells, fraudsters, and emergent noetic beings deliberately copy the same cultural archetypes. The request for invitation is sometimes supernatural folklore, sometimes a legal/noetic consent requirement, and sometimes social engineering. A Black Operator's clothing and speech are deliberately generic because the body may have been assembled from an outdated cultural model. The game never treats all Men in Black reports as one organization.

myth_systems.title: Cattle mutilations and biological sampling
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Livestock mutilation reports produced genuine law-enforcement concern and FBI records in the 1970s. Investigations also documented scavenging, decomposition, media amplification, jurisdictional limits, and competing satanic, criminal, government, and alien interpretations.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A/B for records and investigations; D/E for a universal alien-harvesting program.

fictional_adaptation.name: The Tissue Ledger
fictional_adaptation.summary: Several actors sample livestock for different reasons: Xenos monitor engineered pathogens and reproductive compatibility. Humans run covert environmental surveillance. Machines inspect ecosystem contamination. Pirates steal genetic patents. ordinary scavenging and decomposition account for many cases. The horror comes from realizing that some cases are prosaic, some criminal, and a very small number are strategic sampling - but no visual wound pattern alone settles which.

myth_systems.title: Crop circles, coded messages, and performative evidence
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Modern crop-circle culture expanded rapidly in the late twentieth century. Doug Bower and Dave Chorley publicly demonstrated human construction methods and claimed many early English formations. Later artists, advertisers, hoaxers, believers, and tourists continued the phenomenon.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A/C for human art and hoax history; E for treating geometric complexity alone as proof of extraterrestrial origin.

fictional_adaptation.name: Public-Key Landscapes
fictional_adaptation.summary: Pirates and resistance groups use field-scale patterns as temporary authentication keys visible to orbital sensors. Human artists unknowingly recreate fragments of Machine geometry because both use efficient symmetry. Xeno operations deliberately commission obvious hoaxes around one genuine signal. A formation can be human-made and still carry a real message inserted by a third party.

myth_systems.title: Ghost lights, plasmoids, and persistent anomaly zones
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Hessdalen, Marfa, Brown Mountain, and similar light traditions show how location-based phenomena can be culturally stable while individual observations have different causes. Marfa and Brown Mountain observations often resolve to headlights, trains, fires, or atmospheric effects. Hessdalen remains a continuing instrumented research location with several natural hypotheses and no consensus covering every report.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A/B for measured lights and scientific monitoring; no alien attribution.

fictional_adaptation.name: Luminous Ecologies
fictional_adaptation.summary: Some lights are ordinary optics. Some are natural plasma or geochemical effects. Some are Old Weather status signals. Some are noetic organisms that evolved around strong electromagnetic environments. Persistent monitoring stations become game research sites where the player improves evidence quality instead of simply defeating an enemy.

myth_systems.title: Skinwalker-style anomaly zones
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Skinwalker Ranch lore combines UAP, cryptid, mutilation, poltergeist, portal, and military-contract narratives. Genuine program and contracting history must be distinguished from the claims reported at the property and from entertainment products.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A for documented ownership, investigations, and program relationships; B/D/E for specific extraordinary events depending on provenance.

fictional_adaptation.name: Cross-Layer Faults
fictional_adaptation.summary: An anomaly zone is not one monster or portal. It is a place where several systems overlap: old sensor infrastructure; unusual geology and electromagnetic conditions; noetic expectation effects; deliberate counterintelligence; wildlife and environmental stress; a damaged Source-Lattice node. Different reports can be sincere and mutually incompatible because the site changes observers, sensors, and narratives differently.

myth_systems.title: Bermuda Triangle and oceanic disappearance zones
myth_systems.source_genealogy: The Bermuda Triangle became a coherent popular myth through mid-twentieth- century journalism and Charles Berlitz's 1974 bestseller. Investigations found many cases were misreported, occurred outside the supposed triangle, or had ordinary maritime and aviation risks.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A/C for historical incidents and the legend; E for a statistically proven alien portal zone.

fictional_adaptation.name: Route Shadow
fictional_adaptation.summary: Pirate gate traffic creates regions where official transit logs are systematically wrong. The Bermuda myth is not proof of a portal, but it teaches future investigators that mythic geography can be created by selective case aggregation. A real submerged Machine gate lies elsewhere and was ignored because the public had already been trained to look at the famous triangle.

myth_systems.title: Artificial moons, Phobos, Black Knight, and hidden satellites
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Iosif Shklovsky briefly entertained a hollow/artificial Phobos interpretation based on then-current orbital and atmospheric assumptions. Later measurements changed the problem. Black Knight lore similarly fuses unrelated radio stories, images, debris, and ancient-satellite claims into one object.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A/C for historical scientific speculation and space records; E for a verified ancient Black Knight satellite or artificial Phobos.

fictional_adaptation.name: Natural Body, Artificial Interior
fictional_adaptation.summary: Phobos is not wholly manufactured. A natural porous moon can contain later excavated infrastructure. The Black Knight legend is a deliberate attention sink that merges many unrelated objects. A genuine Machine lurker occupies a less dramatic orbit selected for stability and low detection, not the famous mythic trajectory.

myth_systems.title: Zoo hypothesis, dark forest, great filters, and Berserkers
myth_systems.source_genealogy: The zoo hypothesis is a speculative answer to the Fermi paradox in which advanced civilizations avoid overt contact. The dark-forest model is a science-fiction and game- theoretic idea in which civilizations hide because contact may be fatal. Great-filter and vulnerable-world arguments examine why technological civilizations may fail or become dangerous. Self-replicating hostile machines are a longstanding science-fiction and SETI risk concept.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A/speculative scholarship and C for science-fiction history; not evidence of actual galactic policy.

fictional_adaptation.name: Competing Contact Doctrines
fictional_adaptation.summary: The Federation represents a consent-based zoo/quarantine doctrine. Some Xeno Houses practice dark-forest preemption. Humans believe secrecy primarily protects older powers' monopolies. Pirates profit by breaking isolation. One Continuance branch follows a Berserker logic, while most Machines consider it corrupted. No civilization can enforce one policy across the entire galaxy; multiple cliques and local hegemonies exist.

myth_systems.title: Watchers, fallen teachers, and forbidden knowledge
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Ancient and late-antique religious texts contain Watchers, fallen angels, forbidden arts, giants, divine councils, and transgressive knowledge. Modern ancient-astronaut writers reinterpret those beings as extraterrestrials.
myth_systems.evidence_status: C for religious texts; D for literal astronaut reinterpretation.

fictional_adaptation.name: Watcher as Office
fictional_adaptation.summary: **Watcher** is a translation for a legal observer assigned to a developing civilization. Some observers violated noninterference by transferring weapons, genetic techniques, astronomy, or social control. Religious traditions preserve human interpretations of those events but are not technical logs. The same title was used by Federation, Xeno, and Machine observers at different times, explaining contradictory moral portrayals.

myth_systems.title: Behavioral modification, MKULTRA, and the Monarch mutation
myth_systems.source_genealogy: BLUEBIRD, ARTICHOKE, MKULTRA, and related Cold War programs created a real documentary history of intelligence interest in drugs, hypnosis, interrogation, behavioral modification, and covert experimentation. The U.S. Senate held a public MKULTRA hearing in 1977. Later conspiracy culture expanded that history into total personality programming, celebrity handlers, alien-assisted mind control, and a supposed **Project Monarch**. The documented programs and the later Monarch mythology are not the same source layer.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A for the documented programs and hearings; D/E for a single continuing Monarch superprogram that controls public figures, abductees, and entire populations.

fictional_adaptation.name: Cognitive Security Directorate
fictional_adaptation.summary: Human states really did inherit behavioral-science compartments whose records are incomplete. The Directorate can disrupt memory consolidation, manufacture confidence, and create narrow conditioned responses, but it cannot write an adult personality like software. Xeno noetic systems make some later capabilities possible, creating a dangerous temptation to retroactively interpret every historical abuse as alien-assisted. **Monarch** is an Archive War umbrella label combining several real projects, fraudulent therapists, Compact conditioning, and later entertainment mythology. Missions focus on consent, custody of medical records, false-memory risk, and institutional survival.

myth_systems.title: Gateway, Stargate, remote viewing, and psychic warfare
myth_systems.source_genealogy: The 1983 U.S. Army report *Analysis and Assessment of Gateway Process* examined Monroe Institute methods and altered-state concepts. U.S. intelligence organizations also funded remote-viewing research and operational trials under several names later grouped as STARGATE. A 1995 independent evaluation found the material controversial and concluded that remote viewing had not produced dependable actionable intelligence, despite disagreement over some statistical results.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A for the programs, reports, and declassified archive; B/D for claimed anomalous results; not proof of reliable psychic espionage or alien contact.

fictional_adaptation.name: Noetic Reconnaissance Corps
fictional_adaptation.summary: Noetic reconnaissance returns probability-weighted impressions, never a cinematic remote camera. Every session stores tasking, blinding, raw impressions, analyst interpolation, feedback, and later target knowledge as separate layers. Federation choirs can improve coherence, but doing so risks cueing and consensus contamination. Xenos seed emotionally compelling decoy targets that are easier to perceive than the real operation. Machines use remote perception only as a weak input to larger sensor and archive systems.

myth_systems.title: Project Blue Beam and simulated revelation
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Serge Monast's 1994 Project Blue Beam claim proposed that NASA, the United Nations, and hidden elites would use fabricated discoveries, enormous sky displays, artificial voices, and a staged supernatural or alien crisis to impose a world government and religion. No credible documentation establishes a program matching the claim, and its global projection model far exceeds demonstrated technology.
myth_systems.evidence_status: E as an alleged NASA-UN superprogram; C/D as a traceable conspiracy tradition.

fictional_adaptation.name: Revelation Stagecraft
fictional_adaptation.summary: No faction can project one perfect hologram across an entire planet in daylight. Local orbital projection, drone swarms, augmented-reality compromise, noetic identity spoofing, synthetic media, and captured emergency channels can create the *political effect* of Blue Beam. Humans maintain anti-stagecraft protocols requiring independent optical, radio, cyber, and noetic confirmation before recognizing a planetary contact event. A staged invasion can still attract the real power whose identity is being imitated. The fiction uses the anxiety and operational pattern without declaring Monast's alleged program real.

myth_systems.title: Secret space programs, Solar Warden, and the off-world officer myth
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Secret-space-program lore combines classified aerospace development, Gary McKinnon's reported discovery of terms such as “non-terrestrial officers” and “fleet-to-fleet transfers,” later **Solar Warden** stories, alleged exchange programs, breakaway-civilization narratives, and “twenty-and-back” testimony. McKinnon's interpretation is a claim about material he said he saw; it is not publicly authenticated evidence of an off-world fleet. Later lore greatly expanded beyond his account.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A for the existence of classified aerospace programs in general and the public hacking case; D/E for a verified pre-disclosure interstellar fleet, decades-long off-world service, or age-regression program.

fictional_adaptation.name: The Warden Misread
fictional_adaptation.summary: **Solar Warden** originally names a distributed surveillance, catalog, and continuity network, not a fleet. Human black aerospace offices later use the name for a small cislunar patrol force because the public legend provides deniability. “Non-terrestrial officer” can refer to personnel assigned away from Earth, artificial persons, or legacy Machine offices; none of those meanings automatically means alien. Twenty-and-back stories become contaminated memories produced by relativistic service, continuity restoration, trauma treatment, deliberate disinformation, and a small number of genuine branch returns.

myth_systems.title: Moon-landing hoaxes, lunar anomalies, and the artificial-Moon synthesis
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Bill Kaysing's 1976 *We Never Went to the Moon* became a foundational Moon-hoax text. Apollo landing-site hardware, tracks, returned samples, independent tracking, and functioning lunar retroreflectors support the historical landings. Separate “artificial Moon,” lunar-tower, transient-light, and hidden-base traditions were later fused with the hoax narrative.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A for the Apollo missions and later observations of their sites and equipment; E for the claim that the crewed landings were staged; D/E for a wholly artificial Moon or verified alien lunar cities.

fictional_adaptation.name: Apollo Was Real, the Omission Was Elsewhere
fictional_adaptation.summary: The Apollo missions occurred as recorded. The fiction does not vindicate the hoax by secretly relocating them to a studio. Later lunar survey programs discover younger buried infrastructure inside natural geology. A classified omission concerning an unrelated relay becomes attached to the much larger false claim that the entire landing was fabricated. Humans inherit a cultural wound in which authentic evidence and justified secrecy can no longer be discussed without triggering the hoax frame.

myth_systems.title: CERN portals, collider apocalypse, and ritual hoaxes
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Large colliders inspired fears about black holes, dimensional portals, Mandela effects, occult symbolism, and deliberate reality damage. A 2016 video showing a mock ritual on CERN property was a staged prank filmed without official permission, but it was rapidly absorbed into existing portal and elite-ritual narratives.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A for the laboratory, experiments, and documented prank; E for a verified portal to hell, ritual sacrifice program, or collider-caused timeline rewrite.

fictional_adaptation.name: Collider Keys
fictional_adaptation.summary: Particle colliders do not open mystical portals by default. Certain high-energy field geometries can produce a detectable handshake with dormant Lattice infrastructure, which future physicists initially mistake for instrumentation noise. A prank, hoax, or symbolic artwork can become an effective cover because later evidence is dismissed as part of the same joke. The Chronology Court requires collider experiments to publish branch-integrity telemetry after the first genuine causal anomaly.

myth_systems.title: Elite forums, ritualized privacy, and the cabal compression error
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Bilderberg meetings, policy networks, private clubs, think tanks, corporate boards, intelligence liaison groups, and invitation-only retreats are real social institutions with different histories and powers. Bilderberg describes itself as an informal transatlantic forum held under the Chatham House Rule, with no votes or formal policy statements. Their privacy and elite membership make them ideal anchors for New World Order narratives that compress many networks into one governing cabal.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A for the meetings and organizations; C for conspiracy history; E for one unified body issuing binding secret orders to all governments and alien partners.

fictional_adaptation.name: Consensus Without Minutes
fictional_adaptation.summary: The Six Hidden Tables rarely issue direct orders. They create expectations, shared assumptions, access relationships, and coordinated silence. Participants can sincerely say no vote occurred while leaving with an aligned policy horizon. Real power comes from agenda-setting, credential exchange, procurement, and deciding which crisis receives a common interpretation. The absence of formal minutes becomes both a privacy mechanism and an Archive War vulnerability.

myth_systems.title: Demonological UFO interpretations and the Collins Elite story
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Some religious interpreters understand UFO and abduction phenomena as demons, fallen angels, deceptive spirits, or end-times signs rather than extraterrestrials. Nick Redfern's 2010 *Final Events* popularized an alleged government group called the **Collins Elite** that held a demonological interpretation; the book itself did not demonstrate the story as established fact. John Keel's earlier work also connected UFO reports with older folklore and religious manifestations, though through a different ultraterrestrial model.
myth_systems.evidence_status: C for demonological and religious interpretation traditions; D/E for a verified secret government Collins Elite organization with the claimed knowledge.

fictional_adaptation.name: Ontology Cells
fictional_adaptation.summary: Human agencies maintain competing interpretive cells: extraterrestrial, cryptoterrestrial, noetic, Machine, future-Human, deception, and theological. No cell is allowed to convert its ontology into operational fact without shared evidence. A demonological cell may correctly identify predatory noetic behavior while incorrectly explaining its ultimate metaphysics. The Federation refuses to declare whether its noetic science exhausts spiritual reality.

myth_systems.title: Mothman, window areas, and warning entities
myth_systems.source_genealogy: John Keel's 1975 *The Mothman Prophecies* connected reported 1966-1967 Point Pleasant creature sightings, UFO experiences, strange communications, and the later Silver Bridge collapse. Keel's broader work proposed “window areas” where anomalous reports recur and an ultraterrestrial phenomenon that adapts its presentation.
myth_systems.evidence_status: C/D as folklore, witness history, and Keel's interpretive model; not proof that a winged entity predicted or caused the bridge disaster.

fictional_adaptation.name: Warning Forms
fictional_adaptation.summary: Damaged Lattice nodes sometimes emit anticipatory threat patterns through whatever image a local culture can retain. The warning form may be frightening without being hostile. A genuine warning, a later disaster, selective memory, media amplification, and ordinary structural failure can coexist without one proving the others. Cross-Layer Fault missions ask whether an entity predicts catastrophe, causes it, or merely appears where systems are already close to failure.

myth_systems.title: Roswell, crash retrieval, and the body-recovery template
myth_systems.source_genealogy: The 1947 Roswell event began with military and press statements about recovered debris, later official Project Mogul explanations, and decades of evolving witness, body-recovery, MJ-12, and reverse-engineering narratives. The source layers are not one document set: contemporaneous press, official later investigations, witness memories, disputed documents, and popular culture each enter at different dates.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A/B for the documented military and archival history; D/E for extraterrestrial bodies, intact craft, and forged or weakly provenanced retrieval documents.

fictional_adaptation.name: Roswell Fork
fictional_adaptation.summary: The canon does not declare the entire Roswell legend true. The incident becomes the model for a retrieval narrative assembled around a real classified program, later witness testimony, archive gaps, genuine anomaly rumors, and deliberate myth seeding. One displaced operational truth may survive inside an otherwise false body-recovery story: the military had a protocol for nonstandard biological contamination that was created for an unrelated program.

myth_systems.title: Area 51, S-4, Bob Lazar, and element 115
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Groom Lake is historically real as a compartmented test site for U-2 and A-12 aircraft. Beginning in 1989, Bob Lazar publicly described a nearby S-4 facility, recovered craft, alien propulsion, and element 115. The public genealogy fuses an authentic black-aerospace site with disputed personal claims and later secret-space mythology.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A for the site and aircraft history; D/E for S-4 alien craft and Lazar-specific technical claims.

fictional_adaptation.name: S-4 Compartment
fictional_adaptation.summary: Human black aerospace uses genuine compartmentation and cover stories. A later noetic-material laboratory borrows the S-4 designation precisely because the public mythology makes accurate reporting sound derivative. “Stable 115” in fiction is not ordinary moscovium; it is a trade name for a field-stabilized composite whose public nickname deliberately exploits Lazar lore.

myth_systems.title: Rendlesham Forest and the binary-message mutation
myth_systems.source_genealogy: U.S. Air Force personnel stationed near RAF Woodbridge reported unusual lights in December 1980. Lieutenant Colonel Charles Halt produced a contemporaneous memorandum and later audio; decades afterward, one witness published a binary-code message allegedly recovered through hypnosis or automatic recollection. The later code is not part of the earliest record.
myth_systems.evidence_status: B/C for the event record and witness history; D/E for later binary-message and time-traveler claims.

fictional_adaptation.name: Rendlesham Palimpsest
fictional_adaptation.summary: The earliest observation, the Halt memo, later memory work, and the code are stored as four separate evidentiary layers. In fiction, a real Machine navigation checksum is inserted into the legend decades later by a Human source who never witnessed the original event, creating a true code attached to the wrong case.

myth_systems.title: Colares and Operação Prato
myth_systems.source_genealogy: In 1977, residents around Colares and other locations in Pará reported luminous objects and physical effects. The Brazilian Air Force conducted Operação Prato, producing photographs, interviews, drawings, and reports that later entered public archives. The record establishes investigation and reported injuries, not a final object identity.
myth_systems.evidence_status: B for authentic records and documented investigation; D for alien-attack interpretations.

fictional_adaptation.name: Colares Beam
fictional_adaptation.summary: Colares becomes a model for an Archive War campaign where a genuine state investigation, medical narratives, local folklore, witness fear, and incomplete sensor evidence coexist. Several phenomena occur in the same period: ordinary lights, deliberate Xeno sampling, and Old Weather countermeasures triggered by the sampling.

myth_systems.title: Westall, Ariel, and schoolyard encounter memory
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Westall in 1966 and Ariel School in 1994 are distinct multi-witness school cases often paired because young witnesses reported unusual objects. Their interview timing, adult-witness presence, documentation, cultural context, drawings, and later media histories differ. Treating “children said similar things” as one evidentiary category erases those differences.
myth_systems.evidence_status: C/B for documented witness histories; D for extraterrestrial and telepathic interpretations.

fictional_adaptation.name: Schoolyard Protocol
fictional_adaptation.summary: The 2099 Witness Interview Integrity Protocol records the first individual account before group discussion, every interviewer prompt, all drawings with timestamps, and later memory changes. A mission can contain a genuine event while demonstrating that later environmental messages were partly introduced by interview framing.

myth_systems.title: Varginha and the urban creature-recovery story
myth_systems.source_genealogy: The 1996 Varginha narrative involves reported creature sightings, military activity, hospital rumors, and later claims of capture and transfer. The public source chain is dominated by testimony, retrospective reconstruction, and disputed interpretation rather than an authenticated recovery file.
myth_systems.evidence_status: C/D for the witness and media history; E for unverified body-transfer narratives presented as settled fact.

fictional_adaptation.name: Varginha Chain
fictional_adaptation.summary: A frightened nonhuman refugee, an ordinary military movement, a contaminated animal carcass, and a classified Human medical response occur within the same city. The Archive War objective is not to choose one total explanation but to reconstruct which reports belong to which event.

myth_systems.title: Phoenix Lights and the split-event problem
myth_systems.source_genealogy: The March 1997 Phoenix Lights label compresses observations made at different times and locations. A formation of lights crossing Arizona and later stationary lights associated with military flares became one public narrative. Event labels can fuse separate observations before analysis begins.
myth_systems.evidence_status: B/C for reported events and military flare explanations for part of the night; D for one giant craft as a total explanation.

fictional_adaptation.name: Phoenix Split
fictional_adaptation.summary: Event Segmentation Doctrine becomes a core Human investigative tool. Players must separate one night into independently sourced tracks before assigning technology or faction. The fictional solution may include a real transit event and unrelated training flares without making the flares a cover story.

myth_systems.title: Belgian wave, triangular craft, and radar artifacts
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Belgium experienced a major wave of triangular-object reports in 1989–1990. The Air Force scrambled F-16s during a key night. Later technical work on the radar data identified filtering and track-switching artifacts capable of producing apparently extreme maneuvers. The witness wave and the radar artifacts cannot simply be treated as identical evidence.
myth_systems.evidence_status: B for the official response and witness record; A/B for technical artifact analysis; D for extraterrestrial attribution.

fictional_adaptation.name: Kalman Ghost
fictional_adaptation.summary: One fictional triangular platform is present during a broader wave of imitation, misidentification, and sensor artifacts. The mission rewards correctly downgrading anomalous kinematics while keeping the independent visual reports open.

myth_systems.title: Shag Harbour and maritime crash narratives
myth_systems.source_genealogy: In October 1967, witnesses in Nova Scotia reported lights descending toward or into the water. Search-and-rescue activity and official records gave the case durable documentary status. Later retellings sometimes expand the event into underwater recovery or military pursuit beyond what the public records establish.
myth_systems.evidence_status: B/C for the reported maritime incident and response; D for recovered craft or undersea bases.

fictional_adaptation.name: Harbour Descent
fictional_adaptation.summary: The object entering the water is not automatically an alien craft. It may be a Machine rescue capsule, failed Pirate courier, ordinary aircraft-related event, or perceptual convergence. The case introduces transmedium chain-of-custody rules: identify the sensor, water-entry evidence, search area, and recovered material separately.

myth_systems.title: Betty and Barney Hill, Zeta Reticuli, and the star-map attribution
myth_systems.source_genealogy: The Hills reported a 1961 encounter and missing time. Under hypnosis, Betty described a star map later interpreted by Marjorie Fish as depicting Zeta Reticuli. The Zeta attribution is therefore a later analytical layer, not a location named in the earliest conscious report.
myth_systems.evidence_status: C/D for the encounter and hypnosis record; D for Zeta identification and extraterrestrial abduction.

fictional_adaptation.name: Zeta Attribution
fictional_adaptation.summary: The map becomes a navigation projection whose topology depends on viewpoint, epoch, and route network. Several star systems fit after enough assumptions. In canon, “Zeta” becomes a Human intelligence label that outlives the failed original fit and is later applied to unrelated Grey-bodied groups.

myth_systems.title: Pascagoula, hidden recording, and witness sincerity
myth_systems.source_genealogy: After reporting an alleged abduction in 1973, Charles Hickson and Calvin Parker were secretly recorded by police while alone. Their continued distress is often treated as evidence of sincerity. Sincerity, however, is not the same as accurate external attribution.
myth_systems.evidence_status: C/D for documented reporting and witness behavior; D for the reported beings and craft.

fictional_adaptation.name: Hidden Recorder
fictional_adaptation.summary: Witness Interview Integrity distinguishes sincerity, memory confidence, event accuracy, and ontology. A sincere witness may have encountered a noetic projection, medical episode, staged event, or external entity. Covert recording itself becomes ethically actionable evidence.

myth_systems.title: Communion and the standardized visitor face
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Whitley Strieber’s 1987 book and its cover art helped popularize a large-eyed visitor image that overlapped with, but was not identical to, earlier Grey descriptions. Subsequent experiencer narratives developed in a culture where the visual template was already widespread.
myth_systems.evidence_status: C/D for literary and experiencer history; D for literal visitor claims.

fictional_adaptation.name: Visitor Template
fictional_adaptation.summary: Morphology Capture measures how one influential image changes later reports, art, hoaxes, dreams, and interface designs. Some nonhumans deliberately adopt the expected face because it improves recognition; others are misremembered toward it.

myth_systems.title: Alternative 3, elite evacuation, and climate-collapse mythology
myth_systems.source_genealogy: The 1977 Anglia Television mockumentary depicted disappeared scientists, environmental catastrophe, population reduction alternatives, and a secret Mars colony. It was openly fictional but entered later conspiracy literature as if it were leaked documentary evidence.
myth_systems.evidence_status: C/E as a documented hoax and belief-history source; not a factual space program.

fictional_adaptation.name: Alternative Three
fictional_adaptation.summary: An actual 2099 evacuation plan reuses the name because everyone assumes it is a joke. The mission’s central conflict is selection: who qualifies for transport, who controls the criteria, and whether a survival plan becomes population policy by another name.

myth_systems.title: Wow!, BLC1, and the technosignature candidate lifecycle
myth_systems.source_genealogy: The 1977 Wow! signal remains famous as a narrowband radio event without a confirmed repeat. Breakthrough Listen Candidate 1 initially appeared noteworthy before analysis found local radio-frequency interference. Candidate history demonstrates why detection, verification, repeatability, localization, and publication must be separate stages.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A/B for authentic observations and analysis; no verified alien transmission.

fictional_adaptation.name: Candidate Lifecycle
fictional_adaptation.summary: Every signal mission tracks discovery, independent repeat, source localization, contamination review, information release, and political exploitation. A signal can fail the alien hypothesis yet reveal a Pirate relay or Machine calibration tone unrelated to the original excitement.

myth_systems.title: Atacama skeleton and specimen ethics
myth_systems.source_genealogy: The small Atacama remains were promoted in alien contexts before genomic and anatomical work identified them as human. The case raised ethical questions about acquisition, research, display, consent, and the treatment of human remains.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A for human identification; E for alien-body claims.

fictional_adaptation.name: Remains Protocol
fictional_adaptation.summary: No alleged biological specimen can be treated as equipment or faction loot until Human Remains and Specimen Ethics review resolves personhood, custody, consent, and community claims. The protocol applies equally to hybrids, clones, archived embryos, and uncertain nonhuman bodies.

myth_systems.title: Piri Reis, mythic geography, and ancient-map overreach
myth_systems.source_genealogy: The 1513 Piri Reis map is a genuine historical artifact assembled from earlier geographic sources. Claims that it accurately depicts ice-free Antarctica rely on disputed reinterpretation, projection matching, and selective comparison rather than a demonstrated ancient survey.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A/C for the map and cartographic history; D/E for advanced prehistoric or alien Antarctic mapping.

fictional_adaptation.name: Mythic Geography
fictional_adaptation.summary: Maps have three layers: what the artifact depicts, what later interpreters believe it depicts, and what routes future technology overlays upon it. A false Antarctic reading can still point toward a real modern gate because the later interpreter encoded new coordinates into the famous image.

myth_systems.title: Pole shift, crustal displacement, and scheduled reset narratives
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Geomagnetic reversals, polar wander, axial precession, climate cycles, and catastrophic crustal-displacement stories are often merged. Scientific magnetic reversals are gradual and not linked to mass-extinction resets, while conspiracy narratives compress them into one imminent global event.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A for geophysics; C/D/E for sudden crustal resets and planned depopulation timelines.

fictional_adaptation.name: Pole Shift Countdown
fictional_adaptation.summary: The game separates magnetic reversal, geographic pole motion, climate migration, orbital forcing, and Lattice coordinate drift. A real gate-network realignment can occur during an ordinary magnetic transition without the narrator claiming Earth’s crust flips.

myth_systems.title: Eisenhower alien treaties and Valiant Thor
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Retrospective stories claim President Eisenhower met extraterrestrials, chose among agreements, or signed technology-for-abduction arrangements. Frank Stranges’s Valiant Thor narrative describes a Venusian visitor at the Pentagon. Contemporaneous evidence for the extraordinary claims is lacking.
myth_systems.evidence_status: D/E for treaty and visitor claims; C for contactee-literature history.

fictional_adaptation.name: Treaty at the Airfield
fictional_adaptation.summary: Several genuine continuity exercises, diplomatic codenames, and unusual travel gaps are later fused into an alien-treaty story. In fiction, the forged treaty accidentally uses the syntax of a later authentic Accord, raising the possibility of information backflow rather than validating the original meeting.

myth_systems.title: Cydonia, Mars bases, and the face that moved
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Low-resolution Viking imagery made a Martian mesa appear face-like. Later higher-resolution imaging supported a natural landform interpretation. Separate Mars-base and secret-colony lore often borrows the Cydonia image as cultural proof long after the imaging issue is resolved.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A for the landform and later imagery; E/D for an artificial face and secret ancient city.

fictional_adaptation.name: Cydonia Redirect
fictional_adaptation.summary: The famous Face is natural. Xeno and Human agencies repeatedly exploit it as an attention sink, knowing every new claim diverts public and archaeological resources from a genuinely artificial but visually unremarkable subsurface site elsewhere.

myth_systems.title: Future humans, extratempestrials, and descendant visitation
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Future-human explanations recur because large-headed humanoids can be read as speculative descendants and because abduction narratives focus on reproduction, genetics, and environmental warnings. The hypothesis remains speculative and does not explain nonhumanoid reports or prove time travel.
myth_systems.evidence_status: D/speculative for visitation claims; A/F for using evolutionary and temporal modeling as fiction tools.

fictional_adaptation.name: Descendant Claim
fictional_adaptation.summary: Several posthuman clades can send information or rare bodies backward, but they do not represent one inevitable future. They compete over ancestor rights: whether descendants may manipulate histories that produced them, and whether present Humans owe continuity to futures not yet chosen.

myth_systems.title: Deep state, shadow government, and bureaucratic compression
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Real states contain classified programs, permanent civil services, intelligence agencies, contractors, emergency authorities, informal elite networks, and bureaucratic conflict. Conspiracy narratives compress these overlapping institutions into one coherent hidden sovereign. Inside Job satirizes the fantasy by showing a secret organization subject to budgets, layoffs, rivalries, incompetence, and career incentives.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A/C for real institutions and fictional satire; E for one omnipotent total cabal.

fictional_adaptation.name: Cognito Principle
fictional_adaptation.summary: No hidden institution is allowed into canon without a mandate, budget, workforce, procurement chain, legal theory, jurisdiction, oversight problem, succession method, information boundary, error rate, and rival. Apparent omnipotence emerges from source compression, not actual unity.

myth_systems.title: AI interviewers, synthetic witnesses, and manufactured memory
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Human memory is reconstructive, interview methods can alter recall, and modern generative systems can produce persuasive narratives, images, and conversational reinforcement. Future witness records may include synthetic agents, copied persons, memory-edited survivors, and interview bots whose prompts are part of the evidence.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A for memory and AI-mediated misinformation risks; F for 2099 synthetic-witness institutions.

fictional_adaptation.name: Synthetic Witness
fictional_adaptation.summary: Every witness record stores biological or synthetic identity, model version, memory provenance, interviewer prompts, retrieval conditions, and exposure to prior narratives. A copied mind can be sincere, authentic, and still remember an event that occurred only in another fork.

myth_systems.title: Global archive asymmetry and the Translation Horizon
myth_systems.source_genealogy: UFO records exist across national archives with different languages, release laws, metadata, digitization quality, institutional categories, and historical priorities. English-language UFO mythology often overweights U.S. cases because they are easier to search and circulate.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A for archive differences and access conditions; not evidence that one nation knows the hidden truth.

fictional_adaptation.name: Translation Horizon
fictional_adaptation.summary: The Archive War tracks which records are searchable, translated, linked, and comparable. A case becomes globally influential not only because it is strong but because it crosses the Translation Horizon. Pirates trade translation graphs; Machines preserve originals; Humans build open concordances; Xenos poison cross-language identity matches.

myth_systems.title: Lost Age Stack: Atlantis, Younger Dryas, and Gobekli Tepe
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Classical lost-island tradition, real early Neolithic archaeology, and a scientifically contested impact hypothesis later merge into modern lost-civilization narratives.
myth_systems.evidence_status: A/C/D depending claim

fictional_adaptation.name: Lost Age Stack
fictional_adaptation.summary: Keep Gobekli Tepe Human and the impact debate disputed; fictional lost sites must be separate discoveries.

myth_systems.title: Technology-Shaped Sky: mystery airships, foo fighters, ghost rockets
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Sky anomalies are repeatedly described using contemporary technologies and military fears, from airships and Zeppelins to rockets, saucers, and drones.
myth_systems.evidence_status: B/C

fictional_adaptation.name: Technology-Shaped Sky
fictional_adaptation.summary: Translation Horizon: witness vocabulary is a lossy codec, not a literal engineering diagram.

myth_systems.title: Premodern Contact Forms: Watchers and Utsuro-bune
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Enochic fallen-angel knowledge traditions and the Edo-period Utsuro-bune legend provide premodern forbidden-knowledge and communication-failure structures later compared to alien contact.
myth_systems.evidence_status: C

fictional_adaptation.name: Premodern Contact Forms
fictional_adaptation.summary: Use recurrence of narrative structures without declaring the ancient/premodern sources extraterrestrial reports.

myth_systems.title: Engineering Scripture: Ezekiel spacecraft reinterpretation
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Twentieth-century ancient-astronaut authors such as Josef Blumrich recast religious visionary imagery as aerospace engineering.
myth_systems.evidence_status: D

fictional_adaptation.name: Engineering Scripture
fictional_adaptation.summary: A historically unsupported model may accidentally resemble later technology without turning scripture into a technical manual.

myth_systems.title: Vimana Mutation and the Vaimanika Shastra
myth_systems.source_genealogy: Old literary vehicle imagery is often conflated with a modern Sanskrit technical text and contemporary claims of ancient aviation; a 1974 IISc study criticized the described aircraft as aeronautically unworkable.
myth_systems.evidence_status: C/D/E

mythos_operations.title: Automatic Heaven

mythos_operations.title: Radar Awakening
mythos_operations.premise: Unknown tracks surge after a sensor-policy update; commanders must separate increased activity from increased visibility.

mythos_operations.premise: A 1960 social-impact study is rediscovered after a genuine nonhuman artifact is found; one faction cites it as proof of a century-long cover-up while another uses it as evidence that discovery had always been anticipated.

mythos_operations.title: The Bell Moon
mythos_operations.premise: An Apollo seismic phrase goes viral as proof the Moon is hollow just as a real artificial installation is detected in one crater. Players must prevent the small discovery from authenticating the larger false claim.

mythos_operations.title: Red Glow at Aristarchus
mythos_operations.premise: A transient lunar glow is simultaneously logged by a modern sensor, a century-old visual catalog, and a Pirate relay. The three records may describe three different causes.

mythos_operations.title: The Chronovisor Tape
mythos_operations.premise: A machine claims to reconstruct a lost historical event with impossible clarity. The mission is to recover its uncertainty map before political leaders treat the reconstruction as direct video.

mythos_operations.title: Looking Glass Collision
mythos_operations.premise: Two archive branches contain "LOOKING GLASS": one is a documented nuclear command mission, the other an alleged temporal program. A forged cross-reference tries to make them one lineage.

mythos_operations.title: Convergence Is Not Destiny
mythos_operations.premise: A branch-forecast system shows every modeled future passing through one war. The player must determine whether the convergence is physical, model-induced, or deliberately seeded.

mythos_operations.title: The Carter File
mythos_operations.premise: A high-status historical witness report becomes a cryptographic challenge: preserve the witness account exactly while separating what was observed from every later explanation attached to it.

mythos_operations.title: Outside Threat
mythos_operations.premise: A 1987 rhetorical speech is edited into evidence that world leaders knew of aliens. In 2099, the same clip is used to justify emergency planetary unity during an actual contact crisis.

mythos_operations.title: Moonship Citation
mythos_operations.premise: A 1970 speculative article is presented by a Xeno influence operation as a suppressed scientific consensus. Winning requires reconstructing the citation network, not merely disproving the claim.

mythos_operations.title: The Shock Study
mythos_operations.premise: Federation contact is real, but the first Human policy response comes from an old social-science framework built for hypothetical discovery. Whether that framework protects society or scripts panic becomes the conflict.

canon_guardrails.name: No real-world scapegoat becomes an alien faction
canon_guardrails.rule: Jews, Catholics, Muslims, Masons, migrants, racial groups, nationalities, financiers, medical professionals, scientists, and other real populations may not be rewritten as secret nonhuman bloodlines.

canon_guardrails.name: No unified depopulation plan is presented as established history
canon_guardrails.rule: Real coercive programs are named accurately; Agenda 21 and the Great Reset are represented by their public texts; the mega- conspiracy remains E unless evidence changes.

canon_guardrails.name: Fiction does not vindicate the source
canon_guardrails.rule: If the game contains a Serpent Court, that does not make David Icke historically correct. If Montauk has a fictional archive fork, the Nichols story remains unsupported.

canon_guardrails.name: Experiencers are not automatically liars or infallible witnesses
canon_guardrails.rule: Sincerity, memory accuracy, interpretation, and ontology remain separate questions.

canon_guardrails.name: A classified file is not a confession
canon_guardrails.rule: Withholding can protect sources, sensors, privacy, foreign relations, or ordinary defense capabilities.

canon_guardrails.name: A historical religion is not reduced to alien manipulation
canon_guardrails.rule: The Revelation Stack allows transcendence, mediation, translation, institution, spoofing, and emergent belief to coexist.

canon_guardrails.name: Time travel cannot erase consequence cheaply
canon_guardrails.rule: Branch changes produce identity, legal, archival, and moral debt.

canon_guardrails.name: Every major mystery keeps two live keys
canon_guardrails.rule: One conventional and one speculative interpretation remain available until the campaign supplies decisive evidence.
